extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, health policy stakeholders, Medicare rule commenters, and regulated entities (IPPS and LTCH hospitals) and their representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed federal rule establishing FY2027 update factors and related policies for the Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and Long-Term Care Hospital (LTCH) PPS, including statutory calculations, impact analyses, and requests for public comment. Covers market-basket updates, productivity adjustments, quality-data and meaningful EHR user penalties, special rules for SCHs/MDHs and Puerto Rico, and regulatory impact assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) and invitation for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The analyses presented in this Appendix and throughout the preamble of this proposed rule constitute our initial regulatory flexibility analysis. We invite public comment on our estimates and our assessment of the impact of the proposed policies on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe applicable statutory provisions, identify proposed policies, present rationale and alternatives considered; provide quantitative estimates of impacts on small entities (see Table IX) and allow commenters to contest assumptions and estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of small rural hospital for section 1102(b) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 1102(b) of the Act, we define a small rural hospital as a hospital that is located outside of an urban area and has fewer than 100 beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals in certain New England counties are designated as belonging to adjacent urban areas and thus continue to be classified as urban hospitals for IPPS and LTCH PPS analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prepare regulatory impact analysis for small rural hospitals (section 1102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1102(b) requires a regulatory impact analysis for any proposed or final rule that may have a significant impact on the operations of a substantial number of small rural hospitals and that the analysis must conform to section 603 of the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bed-size stratified payment impact estimates (e.g., 0-49 beds, 50-99 beds) and explain drivers of changes (rate updates, uncompensated care offsets, expiration of programs, MS-DRG changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 202 of UMRA requires agencies to assess anticipated costs and benefits before issuing any rule whose mandates require spending in any 1 year exceeding the statutory threshold (approximately $193 million in 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the rule's mandates meet or exceed the UMRA threshold for State, local, or Tribal governments or private-sector costs; this proposed rule does not meet the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism implications assessment (Executive Order 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13132 establishes requirements that an agency must meet when it promulgates a proposed or final rule that imposes substantial direct requirement costs on State and local governments, preempts state law, or otherwise has federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and state whether the proposed rule would have substantial direct effect on State/local governments, preempt states, or have federalism implications; this proposed rule would not have such effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation requirement (Executive Order 13175 and section 1880(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13175 directs agencies to consult with Tribal officials prior to formal promulgation of regulations having Tribal implications. Section 1880(a) of the Act provides that Indian Health Service and Tribal hospitals are eligible for Medicare payments if they meet conditions applicable generally to hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in consultations with Tribal officials on IPPS issues of interest and use input from consultations and comments to inform rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregulatory offset requirement (Executive Order 14192)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 14192 requires that any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least 10 prior regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify incremental costs associated with the rule and, where applicable, offsets from elimination of prior regulatory costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's recommendation obligation for update factors (section 1886(e)(4)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(e)(4)(A) requires the Secretary, taking into consideration MedPAC recommendations, to recommend update factors for inpatient hospital services for each fiscal year that take into account amounts necessary for the efficient and effective delivery of medically appropriate and necessary care of high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the Secretary's recommended update factors in proposed and final IPPS rules and explain how recommendations reflect statutory considerations and MedPAC input.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPPS applicable percentage increase calculation (section 1886(b)(3)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable percentage increase equals the rate-of-increase in the hospital market basket for IPPS hospitals, subject to a reduction of one-quarter of the applicable percentage increase for hospitals that fail to submit quality information and a reduction of three-quarters of the applicable percentage increase for hospitals not considered meaningful EHR users, and then an adjustment based on changes in economy-wide productivity (productivity adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply reductions before the productivity adjustment. Note that application of the productivity adjustment may result in the applicable percentage increase being less than zero. Cite statutory subsections (viii),(ix),(xi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 2023-based IPPS market baskets (rebase/revision compliance with section 404 MMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: In compliance with section 404 of the MMA, beginning in FY 2026 the 2018-based IPPS operating and capital market baskets were replaced with rebased and revised 2023-based IPPS operating and capital market baskets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2023-based market baskets as the base for calculating the market-basket rate-of-increase for FY 2027 and subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IGI forecast and proposed productivity adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, the proposed market-basket update is based on IGI's fourth quarter 2025 forecast of the 2023-based IPPS market basket rate-of-increase (historical data through Q3 2025), estimated at 3.2 percent, and a proposed productivity adjustment of 0.8 percentage point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that if more recent data become available, the agency would use such data, if appropriate, to determine final market-basket update and productivity adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four applicable percentage increases depending on quality data and EHR status
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on whether a hospital submits quality data and is a meaningful EHR user, there are four possible applicable percentage increases that could be applied to the standardized amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly present and apply the four combinations (submit quality data & meaningful EHR user; submit quality data & not meaningful EHR user; not submit quality data & meaningful EHR user; not submit quality data & not meaningful EHR user) and corresponding percentage increases in tables and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCH and MDH update parity with IPPS (section 1886(b)(3)(B)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(iv) provides that the applicable percentage increase in the hospital-specific rate for SCHs and MDHs equals the applicable percentage increase set forth for other hospitals subject to the IPPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same four possible applicable percentage increases to SCHs and MDHs as for other IPPS hospitals; account for program extensions or expirations (e.g., MDH expiration date) when calculating impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puerto Rico hospital payment parity and EHR adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Puerto Rico hospitals are paid 100 percent of the national standardized amount and thus are subject to the same update to the national standardized amount; subsection (d) Puerto Rico hospitals that are not meaningful EHR users will have a reduction of three-quarters of the applicable percentage increase for FY 2024 and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, depending on meaningful EHR user status, Puerto Rico hospitals face two possible applicable percentage increases (example: 2.4% for meaningful EHR users; 0.0% for non-meaningful EHR users under the proposed IGI forecast and productivity adjustment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-of-increase limits for hospitals excluded from IPPS (section 1886(b)(3)(B)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(ii) sets the rate-of-increase limits equal to the market-basket percentage increase for children's hospitals, PPS-excluded cancer hospitals, and hospitals located outside the 50 States, DC, and Puerto Rico (territories). RNHCIs use section 413.40 and also rely on 1886(b)(3)(B)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the percentage increase in the 2023-based IPPS operating market basket to update target amounts for these excluded hospitals (current estimate 3.2% for FY 2027); state that more recent data may be used if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of facilities subject to rate-of-increase updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's hospitals, PPS-excluded cancer hospitals, RNHCIs, short-term acute care hospitals located in territories (U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa), and extended neoplastic disease care hospitals are among those paid under reasonable cost methodology and subject to rate-of-increase limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each facility type and the statutory/regulatory provision governing its update; apply the market-basket percentage increase to the target amount for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS update methodology and quality-data penalty (section 1886(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed update to the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for FY 2027 is 2.4 percent, consistent with section 1886(m)(3) which requires reduction by the productivity adjustment; in accordance with the LTCH QRP under section 1886(m)(5), reduce the annual update by 2.0 percentage points for failure to submit required quality data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish update factors (example: 1.024 for LTCHs that submit quality data; 1.004 for LTCHs that fail to submit quality data). Note that the 2.4% update does not reflect any budget neutrality factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's recommended updates and consistency with MedPAC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary is recommending, consistent with current law and MedPAC recommendations, the applicable percentage increases described (four combinations) for IPPS hospitals and the same for SCHs and MDHs; recommending 3.2% update for certain excluded hospitals and recommending LTCH updates of 2.4% (submit quality data) and 0.4% (fail to submit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how recommendations reflect MedPAC input and statutory constraints; refer readers to MedPAC's March 2026 report for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: MedPAC standard for assessing payment adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: MedPAC assesses the adequacy of current payments and costs and the relationship between payments and an appropriate cost base, and recommends updates to keep IPPS payment rates close to, if somewhat below, the cost of delivering high-quality care efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MedPAC's assessment to inform Secretary recommendations; MedPAC also recommends redistributing Medicare safety-net payments using the Medicare Safety-Net Index (MSNI) and adding $1 billion to the MSNI pool with transitional approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare DSH and uncompensated care payment framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(5)(F) provides for DSH payments; section 1886(r) provides that an empirically justified DSH payment equals 25% of the Medicare DSH adjustment they would have received under section 1886(d)(5)(F) if subsection (r) did not apply; the remaining amount (estimate of 75%) is available to make additional uncompensated care payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer readers to preamble section V for further discussion; consider DSH/uncompensated care policy changes (e.g., MedPAC MSNI proposal) in assessing impacts on hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate updates for operating and capital payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Because operating and capital payments in the IPPS remain separate, CMS continues to use separate updates for operating and capital payments in the IPPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss capital rate updates separately (see Addendum section III) and ensure calculations treat operating and capital updates independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirement to recommend update factors for multiple categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix B provides recommendations for update factors for the IPPS national standardized amount, the hospital-specific rate for SCHs and MDHs, and the rate-of-increase limits for certain hospitals excluded from the IPPS, as well as LTCHs; IRF and IPF updates will be included in separate Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include responses to MedPAC recommendations and clearly state which facility types are covered in this Appendix versus separate documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity impact estimation assumptions (SBA size standard application)
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate the impact on small entities, the rule applies SBA size standards and approximates the share of affected firms and revenues attributable to small entities by assuming small firms represent 46.1 percent of affected entities and account for approximately 1.8 percent of total industry revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these assumptions to estimate number of small IPPS hospitals and LTCHs affected and average per-small-entity impacts; invite comment on these assumptions and estimates.
